g.text: A) One User Clicks "Book" Multiple Times

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - The Problem: An impatient user double-clicks the "Complete Booking"

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: button, potentially charging their card twice and booking two identical

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Client-Side UI Fix: Disable or hide the "Submit" button after the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: first click. This is a good basic step, but it is unreliable because a savvy

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: user can bypass it by disabling JavaScript in their browser.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Idempotency Key (The Real Fix): Create a globally unique ID

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: (reservation_id) for the booking before the user clicks submit. When they

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: click the button, this ID goes to the database. Because the database

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: enforces this ID as a unique primary key, any extra clicks carrying that

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: exact same ID are simply ignored.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: B) Multiple Users Try to Book the Last Room (Race Condition)

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - The Problem: There is 1 room left. User A and User B try to book it

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: at the exact same time. The system checks the inventory for User A (1

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: room left) and simultaneously checks for User B (1 room left). Both are

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: approved, both book the room, and the hotel is overbooked.

g.text: > The Strategy: Split the massive central database into multiple

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: smaller databases (shards), dividing the total traffic load into manageable

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > How to Split: Since almost all queries search by a specific hotel,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: divide the data based on hotel_id. (e.g., Shard A handles Hotels 1-1000,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > The Strategy: Put a high-speed memory layer (a cache) in front of

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: the database to handle the massive volume of "Are there rooms available?"

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: searches. Only send actual booking requests (writes) to the main database.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > The Inconsistency Trade-off: Because the database and cache

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: update at slightly different speeds, a user might see a room available in the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: cache that was just booked in the database. This is acceptable because

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: the database serves as the ultimate "source of truth" and will catch the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 4) Resolving data inconsistency in the microservice architecture

Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > The Hybrid Approach (Recommended here): By keeping the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Reservation and Inventory data in the same relational database, the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: system can use built-in, reliable database safety nets (ACID properties) to

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: ensure that if a booking fails, everything rolls back automatically.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > The "Pure" Microservice Problem: If you strictly separate every

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: service into its own individual database, a single booking requires updating

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: multiple databases at once. If the inventory database updates but the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: reservation database suddenly crashes, your data is out of sync.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > How it works: A strict "all-or-nothing" protocol that forces all the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: separate databases to lock hands and commit to the data change at the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > The downside: It acts like a traffic jam. Because it forces all

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: databases to wait for each other, a single slow or crashed server will

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: freeze the entire transaction process, making it terrible for system

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > How it works: A relay race of smaller, local transactions. If step 3

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: of a booking fails, the system fires off a sequence of automated "undo"

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: messages (compensating transactions) to reverse the work done in steps 1

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > The downside: It is incredibly complex to code and test.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Furthermore, it relies on "eventual consistency," meaning there is a brief

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: window where different parts of your system will show different, conflicting

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: data while the undo messages are still traveling.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
